incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager P1 triggered for cluster-prod-3: multi-GPU inference jobs failing across two hosts. Alert metric: storefront-embedder error-rate spike -> 18%  (job=storefront-embedder, run=job-9243)

Kate (SRE): I see the pager. Timestamps line up with a couple of CUDA host errors in node gpu-03 and gpu-07. Marking impact: ~5% of customer requests currently failing, degraded latency for everyone. @Amy FYI — CS, we should prep a short mitigation note.

Omar (Runtime): Observed repeated NCCL communicator aborts in TP pipeline. Logs show communicators init failing intermittently, then pods hit container restart. Quick excerpt:```
I0317 10:02:12 nccl_init.cpp:214] ncclCommInitRank returned INTERNAL
E0317 10:02:12 tensorpipe.cc:87] NCCL: allreduce failed, status=Internal, reason="ncclCommAbort or cudaErrorIllegalAddress"
E0317 10:02:13 cuda_driver.cpp:412] CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 0x7ffcf4a3
```

Jun (ML Infra): copying fuller log from gpu-07:```
[pid=4211] NCCL INFO comm 0x7f1a2c: bootstrap connect timeout
[pid=4211] NCCL ERROR 7 (UNSPECIFIED) at /opt/nccl/src/collectives/all_reduce.c:123
[pid=4211] ncclCommAbort() called
kernel: container had OOMKilled; kubelet reported OOM event for pid 4211
```

Kate (SRE): Steps I'm running now: 1) scale down the TP pipeline to single-shard for storefront-embedder (reduce inter-GPU chatter), 2) cordon + drain gpu-07 for hardware triage, 3) restart affected pods with NCCL debug env turned on. Executing scale command now.

deploy-bot: Started rollout: scale storefront-embedder replicas 8 -> 2 by user kate.sre (reason: emergency mitigation).

Omar (Runtime): Good call. While you do that, set NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PX (we saw workarounds before) in the pod spec and restart. Also enable prefix/KV cache bypass for this job to avoid stale KV memory pressure.

Kate (SRE): Applying change to a single canary pod first. Command:```
kubectl set env deploy/storefront-embedder NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/storefront-embedder -n prod --selector=app=storefront-embedder --max-unavailable=1
```
Canary coming up, monitoring logs.

Jun (ML Infra): While canary spins, I'm pulling dmesg from gpu-07 and checking ECC errors and driver faults. So far the GPU has a single Machine Check Exception at 09:58 followed by UVM page fault storms. Might be thermal or driver bug. Escalating to HW team if we continue to see ECC.

Kate (SRE): Canary logs show fewer communicator aborts but still occasional cuda illegal address; however the restart pattern stopped, no more OOM kills so far. Rolling canary -> partial rollout to replace other pods. Noting reduced error-rate from 18% -> 6% in last 4 minutes.

Amy (Customer Success): Thanks — I told the 2 top impacted customers we were investigating and mitigated with a partial fallback to single-GPU processing. They asked for ETA for full restore. Can we give a 30–45m window?

Omar (Runtime): 30–45m is reasonable if rollout continues and we don't hit another hardware fault. Longer if hw team decides node replacement is needed. Also will push a temporary routing policy: serve critical traffic through dedicated single-GPU pool to avoid degradation while we confirm stability.

Kate (SRE): Doing a controlled failover: route 30% traffic to single-gpu fallback pool. Command:```
redwoodctl route update storefront-embedder --pool single-gpu-fallback --percent 30 --reason "P1 mitigation: NCCL instability"
```
Monitoring metrics.

Jun (ML Infra): Hardware team confirms ECC counters incremented on gpu-07; they recommend taking the card out of rotation for deep diagnostics. I've set node gpu-07 to unschedulable and will offload remaining workloads.

Kate (SRE): Handoff to night shift oncall @oncall: we have partial mitigation in place: canary env change (NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1), scaled down TP shards, 30% traffic routed to single-GPU fallback, node gpu-07 cordoned for HW triage. Customers notified. Key artifacts: pod logs, dmesg, kernel traces, and s3 path s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3179990001/ . Please continue monitoring error-rate and latency, keep CS notified on any regression.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded: incident P1 moved to SRE night shift queue, incident id INC-317999. Follow-up checklist: postmortem, RCA (hw vs runtime), and rollback plan if regressions occur.

Kate (SRE): Final note before handing off — if you see recurring `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` after rollback to single-GPU, escalate immediately to ML Infra and HW; that pattern indicates memory corruption. I'll file the initial incident ticket.
